As such, when analyzing backsliding and resilience scholars need to move away from focusing solely on particular institutions and actors with presumed democratic functions, as well as assuming that media and expressive freedom will necessarily serve democratic ends. Instead, we advocate analyzing how the participatory media practices of various actors interact with one another via communicative structures within processes of backsliding and resilience. Participatory media practices that prevent democratic breakdown include disseminating early warnings of backsliding, exposing executive errors and corruption, coordinating pro-democratic mobilization, and platforming the opposition, as well as countering disinformation and delegitimizing democratic institutions and processes. We also indicate how participatory media practices may aid democratic bounceback, as well as the challenges involved in reimagining the media infrastructure needed to sustain democratic recovery in the long-term. Thus, we argue that democratic backsliding and resilience should be reconceptualized as profoundly participatory, mediated processes.
items.summary_ko: 본 논문은 민주적 퇴행과 회복탄력성을 분석할 때 정치행위자와 미디어행위자의 구분을 넘어, 다양한 행위자의 참여적 미디어 관행이 의사소통 구조를 통해 상호작용하는 매개된 과정에 주목해야 한다고 주장한다. 이러한 관행은 퇴행의 조기 경고·권력 남용 폭로·민주적 동원·야당의 발언 기회 제공·허위정보 대응 등을 통해 민주주의의 붕괴를 막거나 회복을 지원할 수 있지만, 반대로 민주적 제도와 절차를 약화시킬 수도 있다.
items.title: Political Actors and Their Media Practices: Analyzing the Role of Media Participation in Democratic Backsliding and Resilience

items.abstract: This article makes the argument that design can serve the purpose of transforming power relations in societal transitions. The article discusses diverse theories of power and their relationship to design, whereby it considers aspects of agency, relationality and scale. Using a design anthropology approach, a theoretical framework is defined for the empirical study of power. The framework is operationalized in a local energy transition project in Amsterdam Southeast. In this empirical study, we describe three power relations that were encountered, the design interventions performed, and their transformative outcomes. Finally, the broader implications for design in societal transitions are discussed.

Abhigyan Singh: Amsterdam Institute for Advanced Metropolitan Solutions, the Netherlands

items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 사회적 전환에서 디자인이 행위성·관계성·규모를 고려해 권력관계를 변형할 수 있는지 이론화하고, 디자인 인류학의 분석틀을 암스테르담 남동부의 지역 에너지 전환 프로젝트에 적용했다. 사례에서 확인된 세 가지 권력관계와 디자인 개입 및 그 변혁적 결과를 제시하며, 사회적 전환에서 디자인의 함의를 논의한다.
items.title: Design anthropology for transforming power relations in societal transitions

items.abstract: This article compares agencification in developing and OECD countries, illustrated by the case of Suriname. Findings show that developing countries prefer statutory bodies and SOEs. Motives for establishment are economic development and the provision of collective goods; typical motives from OECD countries are not present. Patronage plays a major role, and governance and accountability relations are generally weak. Based on these findings, existing agencification theory should include motives that are specific to developing countries, such as pressure from international organizations; pay attention to colonial legacies and acknowledge that agencification in developing countries is much less driven by NPM.
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 수리남의 준공공기관을 사례로 개발도상국과 OECD 국가의 기관화를 비교한다. 개발도상국에서는 경제개발과 집합재 제공, 국제기구의 압력 및 후견주의가 기관 설립에 중요하며, 거버넌스와 책무성은 약하고 신공공관리의 영향은 상대적으로 제한적이라는 점을 보인다.
items.title: Executive agencies in developing countries: the case of the parastatal organizations in Suriname

items.abstract: Public-sector classification systems accumulate classification drift, a widening gap between what employees actually do, how their work is described, and how they are compensated. Because classification shapes pay, role comparison, and internal equity at scale, classification drift quietly compounds into measurable inequity. At a large U.S. urban public school district (the District), this drift manifested as 435 employees sharing the title “Specialist” across 24 pay grades ($47,000–$125,000). This article describes PRISM (Progressive Refinement and Intelligence Synthesis Model), a multi-model AI framework developed with a research-university partner’s Data Science Institute that introduces validation friction at high-stakes decision points. Rather than automating approvals, PRISM surfaces disagreement between independent AI models and routes ambiguous cases to human reviewers with a structured evidence package. Across 992 positions, 173 cases (17%) were flagged for escalated review. This article describes what public HR offices, with or without AI, can do to address classification drift.

Martin Renfro: Metro Nashville Public Schools, TN, USA
Wayne Birch: Metro Nashville Public Schools, TN, USA

items.summary_ko: 이 글은 공공부문 직무분류에서 실제 업무·직무기술·보상 간 격차인 ‘분류 표류’가 어떻게 불평등을 누적시키는지, 그리고 이를 식별·검토할 수 있는지를 다룬다. 미국 대도시 교육구의 992개 직위를 대상으로 독립적인 AI 모델 간 불일치를 인간 검토로 넘기는 PRISM을 적용한 결과, 173건(17%)이 추가 검토 대상으로 분류되었다.
items.title: Classification Drift: Decisions Passing Quietly but Compounding Inequity

items.abstract: Existing accounts of presidential particularism emphasize the targeted distribution of benefits to electorally valuable constituencies. This research note demonstrates that presidential particularism can also operate punitively, through the selective imposition of costs on constituencies that provided weaker electoral support for the president. I examine this dynamic through the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), a highly centralized and politicized agency created at the start of Donald Trump’s second term. Leveraging data on nearly 700,000 federal contracts linked to DOGE contract cuts and 2024 county-level election returns, I show that these cuts were systematically concentrated in counties that provided weaker electoral support for Trump. These patterns hold across contract- and county-level analyses. Together, these findings broaden theories of presidential particularism by showing that presidents may use administrative authority to impose costs on electorally oppositional constituencies. More broadly, I demonstrate how presidents can wield administrative power as a tool of partisan punishment.
items.summary_ko: 대통령의 특수주의가 선거적으로 덜 지지한 지역에 선택적으로 비용을 부과하는 방식으로도 작동하는지, DOGE와 약 70만 건의 연방계약 자료 및 2024년 카운티별 선거 결과를 분석했다. 분석 결과, DOGE의 계약 삭감은 트럼프 지지도가 낮았던 카운티에 체계적으로 집중되었으며, 이는 대통령이 행정권을 정파적 처벌의 수단으로 사용할 수 있음을 보여준다.
items.title: The Punitive Dimension of Presidential Particularism

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Donor‐conceived adults are a growing population, mobilizing against the very regulatory arrangements that determined the terms into which they were conceived. In Canada and the United States, where donor conception remains persistently under‐regulated, gamete donation policy has historically prioritized the presumed needs of donors, recipient parents, and fertility clinics, structuring regulation around treatment access and donor supply rather than the long‐term interests of those conceived. The result is a population that bears disproportionate administrative burdens and is now mobilizing through advocacy organizations, legal claims, and the pathways consumer DNA testing has made possible. Yet donor‐conceived adults remain largely outside the scope of policy scholarship. This paper argues that donor conception offers a theoretically distinctive site for the study of administrative burden, policy feedback, and the social construction of target populations. The paper proposes a research agenda organized around the politics of administratively produced populations and the deliberate distribution of administrative burden through policy design.

Ashley Splawinski: Department of Political Science University of Toronto Toronto Ontario Canada

items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 캐나다와 미국의 기증 생식 규제가 기증받아 태어난 사람들의 장기적 이해보다 기증자·수혜 부모·난임 클리닉의 필요와 치료 접근성 및 기증자 공급을 우선시하면서 행정적 부담을 불균등하게 배분해 왔다는 점을 연구 의제로 제시한다. 기증받아 태어난 성인들의 옹호 활동, 법적 청구, 소비자 DNA 검사 경로를 바탕으로 행정적 부담, 정책 피드백, 대상집단의 사회적 구성 및 ‘행정적으로 생산된 인구’의 정치에 대한 연구 방향을 제안한다.
items.title: From Policy Neglect to Research Agenda: Administrative Burdens and Donor‐Conceived Mobilization

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Switzerland presents a most peculiar political system whose institutional idiosyncrasies shape not only the practice of public administration but also the scientific study thereof. This country study presents the development and state of both public administration as practice and Public Administration as a scholarly discipline. It argues that both are largely determined by three properties of Switzerland as a political context and field of study: Semi‐direct democracy turns the administration into an important political actor. The “Milizsystem” (Switzerland's tradition of non‐professionalized, part‐time public engagement) enables hybrid careers between the public and private sectors and produces a structurally weaker political class that the professional administration regularly outmaneuvers. And the small size of the country has pushed the discipline toward international orientation while simultaneously entangling researchers with their object of study. Taken together, the Swiss case illustrates how political institutions do not merely constrain public administration but fundamentally constitute it.
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 스위스의 반직접민주주의, ‘Milizsystem’, 국가 규모라는 정치적 맥락이 공공행정의 실천과 학문을 어떻게 형성하는지 국가 사례를 통해 분석한다. 스위스에서는 행정이 중요한 정치 행위자가 되고, 공공·민간 간 혼합 경력과 상대적으로 약한 정치계층이 나타나며, 학문은 국제 지향성을 띠는 동시에 연구 대상과 긴밀히 얽힌다는 점을 보인다.
items.title: Small Polity, Hybrid Administration, International Research: Public Administration in Switzerland

items.abstract: ABSTRACT This study replicates prior research to examine how rule communication forms shape administrative burden, while also extending their research by investigating how artificial intelligence (AI) services moderate this relationship. AI services are understood to perform two distinct functions: the labeling function, where chatbots output policy rules directly from databases in response to user queries without further processing, and the optimization function, where chatbots collect, analyze, and distill rule information to present users with simplified, prioritized key points. In Study 1, the original research is replicated in the context of natural disaster relief applications in China. The findings demonstrate that bureaucratic language raises learning and compliance costs, stress, and autonomy loss, while complex information structures also increase learning costs, compliance costs, and autonomy loss. These results confirm that rule communication shapes administrative burden across policies, countries, and languages. However, differences emerge compared to the original study, in which bureaucratic language induced stigma and information complexity had no effect on compliance or autonomy loss, potentially due to contextual factors such as the complexity of Chinese logographic writing. Building on this, the extension experiment in Study 2 demonstrates that AI services reduce administrative burden. Notably, and contrary to expectations, the labeling function reduces learning, compliance, and psychological costs, while the optimization function achieves even greater reductions across all dimensions. Collectively, these findings provide empirical evidence supporting the use of AI to improve rule communication and ease administrative burden.

Ben Ma: School of Political Science and Public Administration Shandong University Qingdao Shandong China
Smart State Governance Lab Shandong University Qingdao Shandong China
Luning Xin: School of Political Science and Public Administration Shandong University Qingdao Shandong China
Qi Bian: School of Political Science and Public Administration Shandong University Qingdao Shandong China
Smart State Governance Lab Shandong University Qingdao Shandong China

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 규칙 전달 방식이 행정 부담에 미치는 영향을 중국 자연재해 구호 신청 맥락에서 반복 검증하고, AI 서비스의 라벨링·최적화 기능이 이 관계를 완화하는지 실험으로 분석했다. 관료적 언어와 복잡한 정보 구조는 학습·순응 비용과 심리적 부담을 높였으며, 두 AI 기능은 이를 줄였고 최적화 기능의 감소 효과가 더 컸다.
items.title: A Replication of “It is Not Merely About the Content: How Rules Are Communicated Matters to Administrative Burden”

items.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) as a case of algorithmic governance whose stated purpose, improving federal efficiency, diverged systematically from its operational effect: enabling unprecedented private‐sector access to federal data systems while dismantling the oversight and civil‐service infrastructure that constrains such access. Drawing on state capacity, bounded rationality, organizational learning, and public value theory, the analysis demonstrates that the conventional efficiency‐failure reading, though correct on its own terms, obscures what made DOGE structurally distinct from the Grace Commission, the National Performance Review, the President's Management Agenda, and Program Assessment Rating Tool, and the Government Performance and Results Modernization Act. The article advances hybrid intelligence, structured human‐AI collaboration with protected institutional capacity, as a paradigm resisting both reform failure and algorithmic capture. International implementations operationalize it. The analysis contributes a stated‐versus‐operational‐goal analytic to the AI governance literature and identifies legislative grounding as a precondition for durable reform.

Haris Alibašić: Department of Business Administration Lewis Bear Jr. College of Business, University of West Florida Pensacola Florida USA

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 DOGE의 공식 목표인 연방정부 효율성 제고와 실제 운영 효과인 연방 데이터 시스템에 대한 민간 접근 확대 및 이를 제한하던 감독·공무원제도 인프라 해체의 괴리를 어떻게 설명할 수 있는지 분석한다. 국가역량, 제한된 합리성, 조직학습, 공공가치 이론을 적용한 사례 분석을 통해 DOGE가 기존 효율성 개혁과 구조적으로 달랐음을 밝히고, 제도적 역량을 보호하는 인간-AI 협력인 하이브리드 지능과 지속 가능한 개혁을 위한 입법적 기반을 제안한다.
items.title: The DOGE Experiment: Algorithmic Governance, Operational Capture, and the Case for Hybrid Intelligence

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Representative bureaucracy research has often linked demographic representation directly to favorable outcomes, inferring active representation post hoc while rarely separating the behavioral component presumed to accompany such associations from the representation variable itself. This study addresses such gap by drawing on gender differences in leadership literature to operationalize supportive leadership as one behavioral component associated with female supervisory representation and examine the constituent elements of what has been interpreted as a representation effect. Using gender pay inequality across US federal agencies as the empirical context, the findings show that while both female supervisory representation and supportive leadership are each positively associated with nonsupervisory salaries when examined separately, the association attributed to representation loses significance once both are modeled together. These findings do not suggest that representation is unimportant; rather, they indicate that prior representation effects may partially reflect a behavioral component that has not been separately identified.

Rachel (Soyeon) Cho: School of Public Affairs American University Washington District of Columbia USA

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 여성 관리자의 인구학적 대표성과 그에 수반될 수 있는 행동적 요소인 지원적 리더십을 분리해, 미국 연방기관의 성별 임금 불평등 맥락에서 대표성 효과가 무엇을 반영하는지 분석한다. 여성 관리자 대표성과 지원적 리더십은 각각 비감독직 직원의 임금과 정(+)의 연관성을 보였지만, 두 요소를 함께 모형화하면 대표성의 연관성은 유의하지 않게 되어 기존 대표성 효과가 식별되지 않은 행동적 요소를 부분적으로 반영할 수 있음을 보인다.
items.title: What Does Representation Represent? Disaggregating Demographic and Behavioral Components

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Governments are usually the largest purchasers of goods and services, creating significant opportunities for corruption. We study whether offering training and technical assistance to procurement officials in 50 Ugandan districts prompted them to publish procurement actions on an online public portal, as legally required. Among districts that received the training and technical assistance program, we randomized whether procurement officials received information in advance about their eligibility to earn a public award for adherence to these transparency standards. We use national administrative data across multiple financial years and 134 district governments to evaluate impacts. The training and technical assistance program increased the number and value of procurement actions uploaded several‐fold, while award eligibility did not have similarly large effects. These results suggest that motivation problems may be overemphasized in the fight against corruption. Building capacity in accounting and transparency could provide effective guardrails against corruption.

Alex Bagabo: Department of Social Work and Social Administration, School of Social Sciences Makerere University Kampala Uganda
Brigham Daniels: S.J. Quinney College of Law University of Utah Salt Lake City Utah USA
Mark T. Buntaine: Bren School of Environmental Science & Management University of California Santa Barbara California USA
Paul Bukuluki: Department of Social Work and Social Administration, School of Social Sciences Makerere University Kampala Uganda

items.summary_ko: 우간다 50개 지역의 조달 담당자에게 교육·기술 지원을 제공하고, 그중 일부에게 투명성 기준 준수 시 공적 포상 자격 정보를 사전 무작위로 제공한 뒤 134개 지방정부의 행정자료를 분석했다. 교육·기술 지원은 온라인 조달 공개 건수와 금액을 크게 늘렸지만, 포상 자격 정보의 효과는 그만큼 크지 않아 투명성 확보에서 동기보다 역량 부족이 중요할 수 있음을 시사한다.
items.title: Skills, Not Just Will: Experimental Evidence From Uganda on Transparency in Public Procurement

items.abstract: Fostering change-oriented organizational citizenship behaviour (CO-OCB) is critical for resilience-building in the public sector, yet the psychological mechanisms driving such behaviour among emergency managers remain underexplored. Drawing on a survey of 869 public employees from emergency management agencies in China, this study examines how psychological safety, creative self-efficacy (CSE), and public service motivation (PSM) influence CO-OCB and tests the moderating role of work autonomy. Results reveal that psychological safety and PSM positively predict CO-OCB, whereas CSE unexpectedly suppresses the effect of psychological safety. Notably, work autonomy moderates the impacts of CSE and PSM on CO-OCB. These findings reveal how psychological safety shapes change-oriented behaviour through distinct but interrelated competence-related and motivational mechanisms within bureaucratic contexts. This study advances public-sector innovation theory by uncovering the nuanced role of psychological safety and by emphasizing the importance of public service motivation in enhancing organizational resilience during institutional reforms and crises.
items.summary_ko: 중국 재난관리기관 공공 employees 869명을 대상으로 심리적 안전, 창의적 자기효능감(CSE), 공공서비스동기(PSM)가 변화지향적 조직시민행동(CO-OCB)에 미치는 영향과 업무 자율성의 조절효과를 설문으로 분석했다. 심리적 안전과 PSM은 CO-OCB를 높였고, CSE는 심리적 안전의 효과를 억제했으며, 업무 자율성은 CSE와 PSM의 영향을 조절했다.
items.title: Psychological safety, motivations and change-oriented organizational citizenship behaviour in emergency managers

items.abstract: Abstract Structural injustice remains a puzzling concept despite its increasing prominence. I distill recent theoretical challenges into a dilemma: either structural injustice lacks the normative credentials of injustice given that wrongdoing is inessential, or it is redundant given existing theories that trace injustice to culpable state and other institutional failures. I then develop a novel account of structural injustice, the Complexity View, that unravels this dilemma. The emergent properties of human actions in a complex society explain what is “structural” about structural injustice, specifically how it can arise without (culpable) wrongdoing. Structural injustice is unjust because it is wrong to contribute to social processes that cause harm and to passively accept preventable forms of vulnerability and deprivation as tragic misfortunes. But this account of structural injustice has a sobering implication: while complexity explains what distinguishes structural injustice from other wrongs, it also sets significant epistemic limits on social reform.
items.summary_ko: 구조적 부정의가 가해자의 잘못 없이도 어떻게 발생하며 기존 부정의 이론과 어떻게 구별되는지를 묻고, 복잡한 사회에서 행위의 창발적 속성을 분석하는 ‘복잡성 관점’을 제시한다. 구조적 부정의는 해를 초래하는 사회적 과정에 기여하고 예방 가능한 취약성과 박탈을 불가피한 불행으로 수동적으로 받아들이는 것이 잘못이기 때문에 부정의하지만, 사회적 복잡성은 개혁의 인식론적 한계를 낳는다.
items.title: Structural Injustice as Emergent Disorder

items.abstract: ABSTRACT The early stages of coalition formation remain an understudied area, particularly in centralized, high‐capacity political systems. Examining actor dynamics at this formative stage can reveal how coalitions form and how limited pluralism constrains their development. This study examines how potential coalition members emerge, and what shapes their prospects for consolidation in this institutional context. We study sustainability efforts in Singapore‐ a centralized polity with a history of state‐led environmental governance and a recent rise of sustainability nonprofits. Drawing on interviews with 39 nonprofits, we examine evidence of early stages of coalition formation outside of the state‐led coalition within Singapore's sustainability subsystem. Our findings show that both subsystem structure and actor attributes constrain potential coalitions from forming, owing to limited resource support and venues to formally participate in the coalition and coordinate with peers and the dominant state‐led coalition. Uncertainty in positions and learning orientation of other actors foster caution and complacency, entrenching weak horizontal ties. Additionally, crises can open brief windows for coordination, but these can close as routines and hierarchies reassert themselves. This study advances our understanding of coalition formation dynamics in centralized, high‐capacity, and limited pluralism contexts where contestation often remains limited and subtle.

Mohnish Kedia: Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy National University of Singapore Singapore Singapore
Sreeja Nair: Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy National University of Singapore Singapore Singapore
Yuhao Ba: Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy National University of Singapore Singapore Singapore

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 중앙집권적·고역량·제한적 다원주의 체제에서 잠재적 연합 구성원이 어떻게 등장하고 연합으로 공고화되는지를 싱가포르 지속가능성 비영리단체 39곳에 대한 인터뷰로 분석한다. 하위체계의 구조와 행위자 특성이 자원·참여·조정 기회의 부족, 행위자 간 불확실성과 신중함으로 인해 약한 수평적 연계를 고착시키며, 위기는 일시적 조정 기회를 열지만 기존의 관행과 위계가 재강화되면 그 기회가 닫힌다는 결과를 제시한다.
items.title: From the Margins: Potential Coalitions in Centralized, High‐Capacity States

items.abstract: Building on the core pillars of Humanistic Management–dignity, ethics, and legitimacy–this study examines how these principles were enacted across organizational, community, and societal levels, and how Humanistic Leadership translated a normative vision of business into concrete managerial, social, and institutional practices. Using an exemplary historical single-case study and an abductive approach, it analyzes Olivetti, the Italian company developed under Adriano Olivetti’s visionary leadership between World War II and 1960. The findings identify Olivetti as a historical example of these principles in practice, showing how dignity, ethics, and legitimacy interacted across multiple levels of leadership to foster both business success and social acceptance. At the same time, the case reveals that the long-term sustainability of this model depended not only on visionary leadership and organizational practices but also on their broader institutional embedding. Olivetti’s legacy serves as an analytical lens for critically reflecting on the transformative potential of Humanistic Management and Humanistic Leadership and the institutional conditions needed to support values-based transformation of business and society and challenge contemporary capitalist logics.

Stefania Camoletto: Universita degli Studi di Torino, Italy

items.summary_ko: 본 연구는 인문적 경영의 존엄성·윤리·정당성이 조직·공동체·사회 수준에서 어떻게 구현되었는지, 그리고 인문적 리더십이 이를 구체적 실천으로 전환한 방식을 올리베티의 역사적 단일 사례에 대한 귀납적 분석으로 탐구한다. 올리베티 사례는 이러한 원칙들이 사업 성공과 사회적 수용을 촉진했지만, 그 지속 가능성은 비전적 리더십과 조직 관행뿐 아니라 더 넓은 제도적 정착에도 달려 있음을 보여준다.
items.title: Leading Humanistic Transformation of Business, Economy and Society: Lessons From Olivetti’s Blueprint

items.abstract: With the racial gap in political-electoral participation well established in the U.S., less is known about racial disparities in other forms of public engagement in governance. This study examines racial differences across nine distinct public participation strategies. It also investigates racial disparities in participation across public, nonprofit, and for-profit sector employees. Regressions conducted using five waves of the Current Population Survey Civic Engagement Supplement suggest that Black and White Americans participate in governance in different ways: Blacks opt for less formal and less costly forms of participation, with ramifications for the diversity of voices included in policy design and implementation. However, contrary to our theoretical expectations, the racial disparities are more pronounced among government employees than among employees in other sectors. Public institutions should create more inclusive opportunities for participation, minimize burdens, and provide incentives for engagement among minorities.

Rui Wang: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 미국에서 인종과 고용 부문(공공·비영리·영리)에 따라 아홉 가지 공공참여 방식의 차이가 나타나는지를 검토했다. 현재인구조사 시민참여 보충조사의 5개 시기 자료를 활용한 회귀분석 결과, 흑인과 백인은 거버넌스 참여 방식이 달랐으며 흑인은 덜 공식적이고 비용이 낮은 참여를 선호했고, 이러한 인종 격차는 다른 부문보다 공공부문 종사자에서 더 크게 나타났다.
items.title: Examining the Role of Race and Sector of Employment in Public Participation

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Does the level of evidence that accompanies policy action depend on how a problem is framed, and on who frames it? This article examines these questions in the context of health crises. Bridging sociological and equivalence framing theories, it treats frames as preexisting interpretive schemes shared within communities of actors, whose downstream influence depends on the information available. Using a comprehensive textual database of COVID‐19 press conferences held in Quebec, where political decision‐makers held greater authority, and in Sweden, where scientists enjoyed more autonomy, the study combines natural language processing, OLS regressions, and Granger causality tests to analyze how frames and disclosed evidence were articulated with suppression and mitigation policies. Findings show that in Quebec, framing the pandemic as an imminent danger was associated with far‐reaching suppression measures even at low levels of disclosed evidence, while the moderate frame's association with mitigation strengthened as evidence increased. In Sweden, no relationship between framing and suppression policies appeared in public communications; framing instead operated jointly with evidence, the dangerous frame being associated with fewer mitigation references mainly at high levels of disclosed evidence. These results suggest that the relevant question is not how much evidence policy action requires, but by whom that evidence is required, and under what conditions. The evidentiary threshold attached to a frame appears to be a property of the community that carries it, with direct implications for how democratic institutions allocate influence between accountability and expertise.

Antoine Claude Lemor: Political Science Department Université de Sherbrooke Sherbrooke Canada
Eric Montpetit: Political Science Department Université de Montréal Montréal Canada

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 보건위기에서 문제의 프레임과 프레임을 제시하는 주체에 따라 정책 조치를 뒷받침하는 증거 수준이 달라지는지를 분석했다. 퀘벡과 스웨덴의 코로나19 기자회견 텍스트에 자연어처리, OLS 회귀, 그레인저 인과성 검정을 적용한 결과, 퀘벡에서는 ‘임박한 위험’ 프레임이 낮은 공개 증거 수준에서도 강력한 억제정책과 연관된 반면, 스웨덴에서는 프레임과 억제정책의 관계가 나타나지 않고 증거 수준과 결합해 완화정책 관련성이 달라졌다.
items.title: Beyond Evidence: How Framing Shapes Public Health Policies During Health Crises

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Central to theories of agenda setting is the distinction between problems and solutions. Kingdon's multiple streams framework argues these processes are rhetorical and have distinct logics and incentives, yet empirical research struggles to measure them separately in digital, elite communication. Legislators bridge the multiple streams through their representational styles and legislative behavior, yet we lack scalable tools for identifying when elites frame issues as problems and when they promote solutions. This research note introduces a machine learning approach for classifying elite communication according to this core agenda‐setting distinction. We develop and validate a supervised model for 1.68 million tweets from U.S. Senators that categorizes messages into problem and solution frames, demonstrating that the problem/solution distinction can be reliably automated. This methodological research note establishes that the distinction is empirically measurable at scale and offers a validated, dataset‐specific measurement approach and theoretical foundation for classifying senatorial Twitter communication as problems or solutions.

Annelise Russell: Martin School of Public Policy & Admin University of Kentucky Lexington Kentucky USA

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 미국 상원의원 트윗에서 의제설정의 문제 프레임과 해결책 프레임을 어떻게 확장 가능하게 식별할 수 있는지 묻는다. 168만 건의 트윗에 지도학습 분류모형을 개발·검증한 결과, 두 프레임의 구분을 신뢰성 있게 자동화할 수 있음을 보였다.
items.title: Problem and Solution Framing in Senate Tweets: Scaling Expert Interpretation With Machine Learning

items.abstract: ABSTRACT A prior experiment conducted in Italy examined how individuals navigate trade‐offs among money, life, and freedom during government‐mandated lockdowns. This study replicates that experiment across three Confucian societies: Shanghai (China), Singapore, and Taipei (Taiwan). The findings indicate that, in the aggregate sample, the preference pattern of “money > life > freedom” mirrors that reported in the original study. However, when analyzed separately, residents of Taipei show stronger preferences for income and freedom than their counterparts in Singapore and Shanghai. Conversely, Singaporeans demonstrate heightened concern regarding the loss of life. In addition to replicating previous findings, this study contributes to the field of comparative public administration by highlighting the importance of considering contextual nuances in the formulation of crisis‐management practices by public managers.

Binzizi Dong: Centre for Public Affairs and Law City University of Hong Kong Kowloon Hong Kong
Chih‐Wei Hsieh: Department of Public and International Affairs City University of Hong Kong Kowloon Hong Kong
Chung‐An Chen: Public Policy and Global Affairs Programme, School of Social Sciences Nanyang Technological University Singapore Singapore

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 공중보건 위기에서 사람들이 돈·생명·자유 간 상충관계를 어떻게 선택하는지 알아보기 위해, 이탈리아의 기존 이산선택실험을 상하이·싱가포르·타이베이의 유교권 사회에서 반복했다. 전체 표본에서는 ‘돈>생명>자유’ 선호가 재현되었지만, 타이베이 주민은 소득과 자유를, 싱가포르 주민은 생명 손실을 상대적으로 더 중시했다.
items.title: A Replication of “Your Money, Your Life, or Your Freedom? A Discrete Choice Experiment on Trade‐Offs During a Public Health Crisis”

items.abstract: ABSTRACT This article presents a 150‐year longitudinal analysis of the development of municipally owned corporations (MOCs) in Sweden, tracing their emergence in the mid‐nineteenth century, their expansion during the growth of the welfare state, and their transformation in the era of market‐oriented public sector reform. While MOCs are commonly discussed in relation to New Public Management (NPM) and contemporary forms of hybrid governance, this perspective overlooks their much longer historical trajectory. Drawing on three major Swedish government inquiries (1924, 1965, and 1982), complemented by secondary historical sources, we examine how MOCs have evolved across changing political, economic, and administrative contexts. The article conceptualizes MOCs as constitutional hybrids, organizations that combine elements of public authority and corporate governance by design, and employs insights from institutional theory and historical institutionalism to analyze their long‐term development. The findings identify three historical phases characterized by changing functions, governance rationales, and institutional expectations. Across these periods, MOCs were repeatedly reinterpreted and adapted to new circumstances while maintaining their basic organizational form. The study contributes to the literature on hybridity by demonstrating that hybridity should be understood not merely as a contemporary consequence of public sector reform, but as a historically evolving institutional condition. We argue that the enduring presence of MOCs reflects the adaptive capacity of hybrid organizational forms, whose flexibility allows them to accommodate shifting demands for efficiency, legitimacy, accountability, and public value. By historicizing hybridity, the article offers a new perspective on institutional resilience, and the long‐term evolution of public governance.

Anna Thomasson: Department of Accounting Copenhagen Business School Copenhagen Denmark
Olof Hallonsten: School of Economics and Management Lund University Lund Sweden

items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 스웨덴 지방공기업의 150년 발전을 어떻게 설명할 수 있는지, 그리고 이들의 혼종성이 현대 공공부문 개혁의 산물에만 해당하는지를 묻는다. 1924·1965·1982년 정부 조사와 역사적 2차 자료를 역사적 제도주의 관점에서 분석한 결과, 지방공기업은 세 역사적 국면에서 기능과 통치 논리가 재해석되면서도 기본 형태를 유지했으며, 혼종적 조직 형태의 제도적 적응력과 회복력을 보여주었다.
items.title: The 150‐Year‐Old Hybrid Organization: A Historical View on Municipally Owned Corporations ( MOC ) in Sweden

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Since the start of the COVID ‐19 pandemic, many countries have been using artificial intelligence ( AI ) to replace civil service personnel. We argue that this practice undermines core democratic values. Using the public values framework, we identify four clusters of values that are threatened when bureaucratic discretion is transferred to algorithms: accountability, fairness and equity, individual consideration, and reason‐giving. Each of these values is incompatible with how algorithms render decisions. Because algorithms produce outputs based on statistical regularities, they diffuse responsibility across multiple parties, fail to make accurate predictions about anomalous cases, and attenuate citizens' claims to individualized consideration. Thus, this article frames AI adoption as a constitutional question about which decisions can be automated, and which should remain under human control because they implicate democratic values. We propose a centaur model in which AI supports rather than replaces human officials, which can preserve efficiency while protecting democratic governance.

L. Jason Anastasopoulos: University of Georgia Athens Georgia USA

items.summary_ko: 코로나19 이후 공무원을 AI로 대체하는 관행이 민주적 가치를 훼손하는지 공공가치 프레임워크로 분석한다. 알고리즘에 재량을 이전하면 책무성, 공정성과 형평성, 개별적 고려, 이유 제시가 약화될 수 있으므로, AI가 공무원을 대체하기보다 지원하는 ‘켄타우로스’ 모형을 제안한다.
items.title: Artificial Intelligence, Bureaucratic Discretion, and Democratic Administration

items.abstract: This study draws on 87 in-depth interviews with frontline workers specializing in social assistance services in Shanghai, China to examine how digitalization reconfigures street-level bureaucracy. Integrating role theory and job crafting theory, we find that digital platforms could produce multiple forms of role strain: redundant labour and fragmented systems generate role overload; misalignment between algorithmic rules and clients’ lived circumstances triggers role conflict; and emotional exhaustion coupled with the erosion of occupational identity results in role alienation. To ensure effective grassroots operation, frontline workers proactively engage in task, relational, and cognitive crafting, sustaining professional resilience despite constrained autonomy. This study critiques digital systems design for overlooking frontline implicit knowledge and suggests that digitalization in the street-level bureaucracy is an ongoing process of socio-technical alignment. The findings indicate that the design-reality gap in digital welfare reform may be bridged by systematically incorporating frontline knowledge.
items.summary_ko: 중국 상하이 사회부조 일선 종사자 87명을 심층 인터뷰해 디지털화가 일선 관료제의 역할 긴장을 어떻게 재구성하는지 분석한 결과, 디지털 플랫폼은 업무 과부하·역할 갈등·역할 소외를 유발했지만 종사자들은 과업·관계·인지적 잡 크래프팅으로 전문적 회복탄력성을 유지했다.
items.title: Role strain and job crafting in China’s digitalizing street-level bureaucracy

items.abstract: Many policies require citizens to actively participate in their implementation in order to be successful, a situation referred to as citizen coproduction. Though citizen coproduction is necessary in many policy areas, it could create difficulties for democratic accountability because citizens and politicians share responsibility for policy failures and attribution of blame may be difficult. We analyze the problem of democratic accountability with citizen coproduction in the context of a model in which politicians, who vary with respect to their competence at selecting policies, choose whether to implement policies whose success depends on citizen coproduction choices. For citizens, the problem is one of attribution: when coproduction is low, it may be hard to select good incumbents because policy failures are frequent even when policy choices are good. Incumbents anticipate these effects, which sometimes implies that they are less likely to choose reforms when they are more likely to be successful.
items.summary_ko: 시민 공동생산에 의존하는 정책에서 정치인의 역량과 시민 참여가 정책 실패의 책임 귀속과 민주적 책무성에 어떤 영향을 미치는지 이론 모형으로 분석한다. 시민 공동생산이 낮으면 좋은 정책을 선택한 현직자도 실패를 겪어 평가받기 어려우며, 그 결과 현직자는 성공 가능성이 높을수록 개혁을 덜 선택할 수 있음을 보인다.
items.title: Democratic Accountability with Citizen Coproduction

items.abstract: Abstract This article investigates Mary Astell’s controversial comparison of marriage to slavery. While existing scholarship situates this analogy within the neo-Roman republican framework, which defined slavery as subjection to absolute rule, I investigate another paradigm: the transatlantic slave trade. To make this case, the article traces the influence of Aphra Behn’s Oroonoko (1688) on early feminist thought. By foregrounding the market logic underpinning chattel slavery, Behn popularized the idea that slavery’s harms were rooted, not in absolute power, but in the commodification of human beings. Astell appropriated this insight, showing that marriage resembled slavery not because husbands wielded power over wives but because the institution had been commodified: women were treated as things to be bought and sold. In uncovering this genealogy of feminist thought, the article highlights the enduring contributions of the “first” English feminists—insights that are entangled with, and shaped by, the development of the slave trade.
items.summary_ko: 이 글은 메리 애스텔이 결혼을 노예제에 비유한 이유를 대서양 노예무역의 맥락에서 재검토하며, 애프라 벤의 『오루노코』가 초기 페미니즘 사상에 미친 영향을 추적한다. 그 결과 애스텔은 결혼이 남편의 절대적 권력 때문이 아니라 여성이 사고팔리는 물건으로 취급되는 상품화된 제도라는 점에서 노예제와 유사하다고 보았다는 점을 제시한다.
items.title: Marriage as Slavery: Oroonoko, the Slave Trade, and the Origins of English Feminism

items.abstract: Calls to “democratize finance” abound today. Yet this apparent consensus obscures sharply divergent conceptions of both democracy and finance. This article maps these demands along two axes, distinguishing between access- and power-based conceptions of democracy, and between three dimensions of finance: payment, capital markets, and banking. We then develop three normative claims. First, we argue that conceptions that reduce democratization to expanded market access are not merely insufficient but, when applied to speculative capital markets, amount to predatory inclusion. Second, thicker accounts of democratization as equal inclusion are normatively more promising but internally unstable, as their democratic commitments generate pressures toward power sharing. Third, the most plausible conceptions of democratizing finance are power-centered and involve greater public control over credit creation and allocation. Rather than defending a single institutional solution, the article assesses a range of reform proposals while specifying a normative threshold for evaluating what it would mean to democratize finance.
items.summary_ko: 이 글은 민주주의와 금융에 대한 상이한 개념을 바탕으로 ‘금융의 민주화’ 요구를 어떻게 평가할 것인지 묻고, 민주주의를 접근·권력 중심으로, 금융을 결제·자본시장·은행의 세 차원으로 구분해 개념적으로 분석한다. 시장 접근 확대만을 민주화로 보는 관점은 특히 투기적 자본시장에서 약탈적 포용이 될 수 있으며, 가장 설득력 있는 구상은 신용 창출과 배분에 대한 공적 통제를 강화하는 권력 중심 접근이라고 주장한다.
items.title: What Would It Mean to Democratize Finance? An Evaluation of Divergent Conceptions of Democracy and Finance

items.abstract: This study examines how organizational factors shaped telemedicine equity outcomes across 623 public hospitals in Chile, Mexico, Colombia, Ecuador, and Uruguay from 2015 to 2025. Using hospital-year data from ministry databases, PAHO registries, waiting-time records, audit reports, training logs, and technology-readiness assessments, the analysis combines descriptive statistics, multilevel regression, difference-in-differences estimation, country-level models, and a limited instrumental-variable sensitivity analysis. Results show that the rural–urban specialist waiting-time gap declined from 5.1 to 1.9 days after telemedicine expansion. Centralized implementation was associated with a 0.187-unit improvement in the Access Equity Index, while each additional 10 hours of staff training was associated with a 0.024-unit improvement. Findings suggest that telemedicine equity depends not only on technology adoption, but also on organizational coordination, workforce preparation, and implementation capacity within public health systems.
items.summary_ko: 본 연구는 칠레·멕시코·콜롬비아·에콰도르·우루과이 공공병원 623곳의 2015~2025년 병원-연도 자료를 활용해 조직 요인이 원격의료의 접근 형평성에 어떤 영향을 미쳤는지 다층회귀, 이중차분 및 제한적 도구변수 분석으로 검토했다. 원격의료 확대 후 농촌-도시 전문의 대기시간 격차가 감소했으며, 중앙집중형 실행과 직원 교육시간 증가는 접근 형평성 개선과 관련됐다.
items.title: Organizational Determinants of Telemedicine Equity Outcomes in Latin American Public Health Systems

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Many critical infrastructure services operate within quasi‐regulated (i.e., “deregulated”) markets. Public managers face a unique set of challenges and opportunities in the administration and oversight of these markets. Administrative and regulatory challenges exist because public managers are required to balance an open and competitive marketplace while confronting multiple market failures (e.g., consumer inattention, imperfect competition) alongside organizational, management, and legal and regulatory enforcement challenges. There are real‐world consequences of administrative choices on economic (in)efficiency and consumer equity. This paper provides public managers with a comprehensive review of the public management challenges and opportunities associated with managing deregulated retail electricity markets. It then provides a review of empirical research and an empirical example for one category of these challenges—consumer equity. The paper concludes with a multi‐disciplinary discussion of the role of public managers in deregulated marketplaces and public policy options to address both equity and efficiency challenges.
